### For Such a Time as This
Author: Emma Danzey
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/for-such-a-time-as-this-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Esther 4:14
Points:
- Believers are often tempted to stay quiet about their faith out of fear or intimidation.
- Keeping silent does not ensure personal safety and forfeits the chance to be used by God.
- If we refuse God's call to act, He will accomplish His purposes through someone else.
- God intentionally places each Christian into their specific generation and circumstances for His glory.

### For Such a Time as This
Author: Debbie McDaniel
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/crosswalk-the-devotional-january-17.html
Passage: Esther 4:14
Points:
- God has the power to transform difficult trials and uncertainty into greater purpose.
- Esther chose to seek God through prayer and fasting rather than staying paralyzed by fear.
- Believers are frequently placed in strategic locations to serve God's broader redemptive plan.
- Facing dark times requires surrendering control to God and stepping forward in obedience.

### Such a Time as This
Author: Jana Kelley
Site: Wholly Loved Ministries (Crosswalk.com)
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/wholly-loved/wholly-loved-feb-28.html
Passage: Esther 4:14
Points:
- Difficult circumstances can make believers want to retreat and hide from reality.
- Despite being an exiled orphan in a foreign palace, Esther was placed there by God.
- Mordecai recognized Esther's potential and challenged her to take a courageous stand.
- God intentionally positions and equips every believer to take faith-filled risks for His kingdom.

### For Such a Time as This
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/such-time
Passage: Esther 4:14
Points:
- Esther and Mordecai were imperfect believers whose motives were not always pure.
- God works through flawed people and complex situations to advance His redemptive will.
- Divine providence is often concealed, meaning believers rarely know outcomes in advance.
- Faith requires doing what is right according to God's Word even amid uncertain results.
